items.title: Fake Bill-Payment Websites Are Tricking You Through Search Ads
items.summary: The FTC just warned that scammers are buying fake ads at the top of Google and Bing that look like your electric company, insurance provider, or bank. You search for "pay my light bill," click the first result, enter your account number and card, and the money goes to a crook instead of your real company. Always scroll past the ads and look for the official web address you already know — or call the number on your paper bill. Report fraud at ReportFraud.ftc.gov. (Source: FTC.gov, August 17, 2026)

items.title: Stop Windows from begging you to buy Microsoft 365 — turn off the subscription nag screens
items.summary: Press the Windows key, type **Notifications** and press Enter. Scroll down and turn off notifications from **Microsoft 365 (Office)** and **Get Help**. That kills the pop-ups permanently — takes 30 seconds.

items.title: Turn your old scanner into a clean PDF maker — NAPS2 is free and has no watermarks
items.summary: Download **NAPS2** (Not Another PDF Scanner 2) free at **naps2.org**. Plug in your scanner, open NAPS2, click the green **Scan** button, and save your document as a PDF or image file. No account, no watermarks, no ads, no subscription.

items.title: Microsoft Edge Browser Security Update — Check Yours in 30 Seconds Free
items.summary: Microsoft pushed a fresh security patch to Edge this week that closes several vulnerabilities attackers are actively exploiting through malicious websites. If your Edge browser is out of date, simply visiting the wrong page could let someone run code on your computer. Here's the fix — it's free and takes 30 seconds: open Microsoft Edge, click the three dots in the top right corner, choose Help and feedback, then About Microsoft Edge. The browser will show your current version and update automatically if it's not current. I do this check on every computer that comes into the shop, and I'm always surprised how many are months behind. Don't be one of them — check it now. (Source: Microsoft Security Response Center, August 2026)

items.title: Microsoft Edge just got a security update — check yours free in 30 seconds at edge://settings/help
items.summary: Microsoft pushed a fresh security patch to Edge this week. Open Microsoft Edge, click the three dots in the top right, choose Help and feedback, then About Microsoft Edge — it will show your current version and update automatically if it's not current. Takes 30 seconds.

items.title: Find any file in a second — Everything Search by Voidtools is free and finds what Windows Search misses at voidtools.com
items.summary: Windows Search is slow and sometimes misses files entirely. Everything Search by Voidtools indexes your entire drive the moment you install it and finds any file the instant you type its name. Download it free from voidtools.com — no account needed, no ads, takes 2 minutes to install.

items.title: Healthcare Company CareCloud Confirms Data Breach Affecting 3.7 Million Patients
items.summary: Healthcare technology company CareCloud confirmed a massive data breach that exposed personal information of 3.7 million patients, according to a report by BleepingComputer on August 19, 2026. If you or a family member received care from a medical provider that uses CareCloud systems, your name, contact details, and health-related information may have been compromised. Here's what to do right now: call your healthcare provider's office and ask if they use CareCloud, then place a free fraud alert on your credit reports by calling Equifax at 1-800-525-6285, Experian at 1-888-397-3742, or TransUnion at 1-800-680-7289.

items.title: Government warns ransomware gangs are targeting Windows computers right now — Windows Update keeps you safe
items.summary: CISA (the government's cybersecurity agency) confirmed that ransomware gangs are actively using a Windows flaw to take full control of computers. Open Settings, click Windows Update, and click "Check for updates" — it takes 2 minutes and keeps you safe.

items.title: Adobe Firefly now generates music, speech, and sound effects free — try it at firefly.adobe.com
items.summary: Adobe's free AI tool Firefly can now create background music, voice narration, and sound effects from a simple text description. Go to firefly.adobe.com, sign up free with any email, and click "Generate Audio" — no music skills needed, and you get free tries every day.

items.title: Scammers Are Posing as Computer 'Rescue' Companies — Don't Pay Them a Dime
items.summary: Crooks are now posing as computer "rescue" companies to steal money. Researchers say a group calling itself Ransom Busters has been emailing people right after their computers are attacked — sometimes before the attack is even public — and offering to "recover" their files for a fee. Researchers believe the "rescuers" are the same crooks behind the attacks. If you get an email or call like this, don't pay, don't reply, and don't call the number in the message. Real help never comes from a stranger demanding money.

items.title: Hackers found a way into Macs over the internet and are using them to mine digital money — update macOS today
items.summary: Open System Settings, click General, then Software Update, and install whatever Apple offers — it's free and takes about 10 minutes. If you can't update right away, you can also turn off Screen Sharing (System Settings → General → Sharing → Screen Sharing) unless you actually use it.

items.title: Your PC feels slow? Task Manager shows what's eating it — built into Windows, press Ctrl+Shift+Esc
items.summary: Press Ctrl+Shift+Esc to open Task Manager — it's built into Windows and shows every program running on your computer. Look at the top of the list: whatever is using the most working memory is usually the troublemaker. To close a stuck program, click it, then click End Task.
